questions.question: Which circuit, home of the British Grand Prix, has this shape?
questions.explanation: Silverstone was built on a Second World War airfield, and some of its straights follow the old runways.

media.alt: A map of a motor racing track

questions.question: This twisty track runs through the streets of a tiny country, past a harbour full of yachts. Which race is it?
questions.explanation: Monaco's streets are so narrow that overtaking is almost impossible, so qualifying near the front matters hugely.

media.alt: A map of a twisty motor racing track

questions.question: Which Formula 1 team has this prancing horse on its badge?
questions.explanation: The horse was painted on the plane of an Italian wartime pilot, and his mother suggested Enzo Ferrari use it for luck.

media.alt: A black horse rearing up on its back legs

questions.question: Which flag is waved as the winner crosses the finish line?
questions.explanation: The black-and-white chequered flag is waved at the winner first, then at every car that finishes behind.

questions.question: In Formula 1, what does a waved yellow flag tell the drivers?
options: Danger ahead: slow down and do not overtake
questions.answer: Danger ahead: slow down and do not overtake
questions.explanation: Marshals wave yellow flags when there is a crashed car or debris near the track.

questions.question: At a pit stop, about how long does a top team take to change all four tyres?
questions.explanation: Around twenty mechanics work on the car at once, and the fastest stops take less than two seconds.

questions.question: In 2020, Lewis Hamilton won his seventh world title to equal the record of which German driver?
questions.explanation: Schumacher won his seven titles with Benetton and Ferrari; Hamilton won his with McLaren and Mercedes.

questions.question: Lewis Hamilton was born in which English town?
questions.explanation: Hamilton started racing go-karts aged eight, near his home in Hertfordshire.

questions.question: Max Verstappen races under the flag of which country?
questions.explanation: His Dutch fans dress head to toe in orange and are known as the Orange Army.

questions.question: What does the F in F1 stand for?
questions.explanation: The formula is the set of rules that every car must be built to.

questions.question: What is the 'halo' on a Formula 1 car?
options: A strong bar that protects the driver's head
A light that flashes in the rain
A ring on the steering wheel
questions.answer: A strong bar that protects the driver's head
questions.explanation: The halo arrived in 2018 and is strong enough to hold the weight of a double-decker bus.

questions.question: In 2008, the Singapore Grand Prix became the first Formula 1 race held when?
questions.explanation: Hundreds of huge floodlights light up the streets so the drivers can see.

questions.question: Since 2010, how many points has a driver earned for winning a Grand Prix?
questions.explanation: Second place earns 18 and third earns 15, all the way down to a single point for tenth.

questions.question: In 2025, which British driver won his first Formula 1 world championship, driving for McLaren?
questions.explanation: Norris clinched the title at the very last race of the season, in Abu Dhabi.

questions.question: What is it called when a driver starts the race from the very front of the grid?
questions.explanation: The fastest driver in qualifying earns pole position.

questions.question: Which Grand Prix circuit, which crosses over itself in a figure of eight, has this shape?
questions.explanation: Suzuka in Japan was built by Honda as a test track, and a bridge carries one part of the circuit over another.

media.alt: A map of a motor racing track

questions.question: Which circuit, with its famous Eau Rouge corner, has this shape?
questions.explanation: At about 7 km, Spa-Francorchamps in Belgium's Ardennes forest is one of the longest circuits in Formula 1.

media.alt: A map of a long motor racing track

questions.question: Ayrton Senna won the Monaco Grand Prix a record how many times?
questions.explanation: Senna won in 1987 and then five years in a row from 1989 to 1993.

questions.question: Which British driver won the 1976 world title by a single point from Niki Lauda?
questions.explanation: Their rivalry, and Lauda's return from a terrible crash, was told in the 2013 film Rush.

questions.question: Jim Clark won both of his world titles, in 1963 and 1965, with which team?
questions.explanation: In 1965 Clark also won the Indianapolis 500 in a Lotus.

questions.question: Juan Manuel Fangio won five world titles in the 1950s with how many different teams?
questions.explanation: Fangio won with Alfa Romeo, Mercedes, Ferrari and Maserati.

questions.question: McLaren's headquarters, the McLaren Technology Centre, is in which Surrey town?
questions.explanation: The building, designed by Norman Foster, sits beside a large man-made lake.

questions.question: Michael Schumacher won his first two world titles, in 1994 and 1995, with which team?
questions.explanation: Schumacher joined Ferrari in 1996 and won five titles in a row with them from 2000.

questions.question: In 1958, who became the first British Formula 1 world champion?
questions.explanation: Hawthorn beat Stirling Moss to the title by a single point, then retired at the end of the season.

questions.question: Which British driver, often called the greatest never to win the title, was runner-up four years in a row from 1955?
questions.explanation: Moss won 16 Grands Prix but finished second in the championship in 1955, 1956, 1957 and 1958.

questions.question: In 1972, who completed motor racing's 'Triple Crown' by adding Le Mans to wins at Monaco and the Indianapolis 500?
questions.explanation: Hill won Monaco five times, earning the nickname 'Mr Monaco'.

questions.question: In Formula 1, what does a waved blue flag tell a driver?
options: A faster car is about to lap you: let it pass
questions.answer: A faster car is about to lap you: let it pass
questions.explanation: Drivers who ignore blue flags for too long can be given a penalty.

questions.question: Which Italian circuit is nicknamed 'the Temple of Speed'?
questions.explanation: Monza's long straights make it the fastest track in Formula 1, with cars passing 350 km/h.

questions.question: Which Finnish world champion was nicknamed 'the Iceman' for his cool calm?
questions.explanation: Räikkönen won the 2007 title with Ferrari, and once told his team over the radio 'Leave me alone, I know what I'm doing'.

questions.question: Jenson Button won the 2009 world title with which team, in its one and only season?
questions.explanation: Brawn rose from the ashes of Honda's team and was then sold to become Mercedes.
